name: 1/4" TRS (6.35mm audio jack)
ascii:
sleeve         ring          tip
        |             |             |
   =====+=============+=============+===>   (insert ->)
        |             |             |
        S             R             T
       GND        Right / cold   Left / hot
description: The full-size 6.35mm phone jack, electrically identical to the 3.5mm TRS but bigger and sturdier. Same conductor order (Tip, Ring, Sleeve). A 2-conductor TS version (no ring) is the standard mono instrument jack: Tip = signal, Sleeve = ground. TRS carries stereo (Tip=L, Ring=R) or balanced mono (Tip=+, Ring=-).

contacts.name: Tip
contacts.description: signal / left (stereo) / hot + (balanced); the sole signal on a mono TS instrument cable

contacts.name: Ring
contacts.description: right (stereo) / cold - (balanced); absent on a mono TS plug

variants: TS (mono, 2-conductor) is the guitar / instrument cable: Tip = signal, Sleeve = ground, unbalanced.
TRS (this): stereo headphones (Tip=L, Ring=R) or a balanced mono line (Tip=+, Ring=-). Same plug, wiring intent differs.
Insert / send-return and stereo-headphone TRS both exist; an insert cable splits Tip=send, Ring=return on one TRS.
gotchas: Instrument cable vs speaker cable: a 1/4" TS instrument cable is thin, shielded, coax; a speaker cable is unshielded heavy 2-conductor. They share the plug but are NOT interchangeable -- an instrument cable on a speaker output can overheat, and a speaker cable on a guitar hums.
Balanced TRS and stereo TRS are physically identical -- plugging a balanced source into a stereo input (or vice versa) misroutes the signal (only one side, or phase issues).
Guitar / synth patch signals on TS are UNBALANCED, so long runs pick up hum -- that's what a DI box (TS -> balanced XLR) is for.
notes: 6.35mm TRS/TS phone jack, same conductor assignment as the 3.5mm (Tip=L/signal, Ring=R/cold, Sleeve=GND). Instrument-vs-speaker-cable warning included.
